class: A value set without the events a React form listens for: the form sent a different value from the box's
symptom: Waystar and Crescent Energy (Workday), 1 October, and KBI before: the account was created, and the agent's sign-in with the same email and password was refused ('You may have entered the wrong email address or password'). No verification email was ever sent; the owner then signed in by hand with the same password at once.
site: Workday, and any React/Vue form whose submit reads its own registered state
root_cause: attempt_auto_login set the email and the password with a bare locator.fill() and never checked them; the Create Account form typed the password key by key and checked it. CLAUDE.md section 3 requires focus -> fill -> input -> change -> blur on every fill; the sign-in was the one path that did not follow it, so the refusals were read as 'unverified account' and 'wrong password' and sent the agent to the mail and to password resets.
why_tests_missed: The sign-in fixtures were plain HTML forms that submit the box's value, so a bare fill() worked there; none registered the value from keystrokes as a React form does.
fix: The email is set with fill_and_dispatch; the password is typed key by key, the box is left (Tab), and its value is checked before Sign In is pressed (_type_password). A password the box did not keep is never submitted.
prevention: One input primitive for every box (fill_and_dispatch, or keystrokes for secrets) and a read-back before any submit that spends an attempt; test forms that keep their own state, not only plain HTML.
